Local Instant Meshes fixture set

Keep the original small grid, sphere and creased patch suite for fast stage
diagnostics. This directory includes broader geometry and matched options for the
parity and performance comparisons.

Generated fixtures
    Torus, 1,920 triangles              Closed genus one, quads and triangles
    Angle bracket, 932 triangles      Sharp convex and concave edges
    Nearby sheets, 2,016 triangles      Separate surfaces and boundary alignment
    Dense torus, 69,120 triangles        Medium benchmark with regular connectivity
    Oriented torus, 960 points          Point-cloud reconstruction with normals

Provider fixtures
    Spot, 5,856 triangles               Clean organic shape with small features
    Stanford Bunny, 69,451 triangles    Scan irregularity and five openings
    Armadillo, 345,944 triangles        Dense scan for time and memory scaling

Spot comes from Keenan Crane's CMU model repository under CC0 1.0. Stanford
Bunny and Armadillo come from the Stanford Computer Graphics Laboratory.
The Stanford repository permits research use with attribution and requires
permission for commercial uses. Keep these benchmark files out of the plugin
package and listing assets. The provider manifest records the original URLs,
attribution, source archive SHA-256, prepared OBJ SHA-256 and target settings.
The adapters keep positions, triangle indices and their order and discard texture
coordinates and scan attributes.

Run the commands in this guide from tests/fixtures. Each fixtures.json includes
the case settings. Regenerate the synthetic files with:

    python3 extended_fixtures.py generated

The source snapshot includes the provider URLs and hashes in providers/fixtures.json.
To prepare the meshes locally, download the three listed archives as spot.zip,
bunny.tar.gz and Armadillo.ply.gz. Use a separate output folder for preparation:

    python3 prepare_provider_fixtures.py ARCHIVE_DIR /tmp/im-provider-fixtures
    diff providers/fixtures.json /tmp/im-provider-fixtures/fixtures.json
    cp /tmp/im-provider-fixtures/*.obj providers/

If the hashes differ, keep the retained manifest and verify the source archives
before using the new meshes. Omit --generated-only to test the provider meshes
after preparation. The historical private mesh requires a separate local input.

Reproduce the stable topology smoke comparison
    1. Set PORT_SCRATCH to the absolute path of a scratch copy of the pinned
       InstantMeshesPort with its vendor sources. Run make parity there.
    2. Compile check/native.cpp against that scratch copy, for example:
       clang++ -std=c++14 -O2 -I"$PORT_SCRATCH/native" check/native.cpp \
         "$PORT_SCRATCH/build/native/libinstantmeshes.a" -o /tmp/im-fixture-native
    3. dotnet build check/managed -c Release
    4. python3 check/run.py --native /tmp/im-fixture-native --generated-only

The runner writes check/results/fixture-smoke.json. Failed connectivity checks
are recorded as false so the remaining cases still run. STATUS.md links to the
historical candidate reports. PERFORMANCE.md records the release timing methods,
results, and reproduction steps at the project root.

Parity on Apple Silicon

Nine of ten stable cases match the pinned port in ordered connectivity and
every coordinate. Both modes of the oriented torus also match the pinned port
on radius, directed candidates, final adjacency and fields. The native
reference runner in tests/reference/run.py traces those stages end to end.

Bunny matches the pinned port in ordinary arithmetic with 10,012 vertices and
9,941 faces at a 2,500-vertex target. The pinned stable result diverges at
level-zero coarsening because its zero-area score comparator is intransitive.
With --reference-score-policy the runner applies the managed area policy to
the scratch C++ build. Stable Bunny then matches all ordered indices and all
positions with 10,001 vertices and 9,927 faces. The two reference reports and
the cycle in the native comparator are in the historical snapshot linked from
STATUS.md.
